entries.name: Overlapping or stale routes
entries.symptom: Multiple routes share the same destination prefix, often after a VPN or virtual switch.
entries.detection: Duplicate destination prefixes or persistent stale routes
entries.explanation: Removes one specific stale route; interface metrics can be adjusted with ADP-06. As a last resort, route -f can clear every route; it breaks VPN tunnels and needs a reboot, and it asks for a second explicit confirmation.

snapshot.label: route table
snapshot.script:
Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Select-Object DestinationPrefix,NextHop,InterfaceAlias,RouteMetric,InterfaceMetric,Store |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4

entries.rollback_notes: The pre-fix snapshot stores the full route table. After removing the specific route, re-add it only if the VPN or virtual adapter needs it; most stale routes should not return. After route -f, routes are rebuilt by DHCP on renew or reboot; VPN and persistent routes must be re-added manually from the snapshot.

ladder.name: Remove the specific stale route
ladder.description: Never clears the whole route table from this step.

ladder.name: Clear all routes (last resort)
ladder.description: route -f deletes every route, including VPN and persistent routes; it breaks active VPN tunnels and requires a reboot afterwards. Use only if removing the specific stale route did not resolve the problem.

entries.symptom: Some sites hang because IPv6 is preferred but not routed.

entries.explanation: Applies the documented IPv4-preference workaround in the Tcpip6 registry and requires a reboot. This is a workaround, not a repair of the IPv6 path.

snapshot.label: IPv6 registry
snapshot.script:
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip6\Parameters' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Select-Object DisabledComponents |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4

entries.name: No default gateway configured
entries.symptom: The adapter has an address but no default gateway, so only local-subnet traffic works.
entries.detection: An active physical adapter has an IPv4 address and no 0.0.0.0/0 route or configured gateway
entries.explanation: NetScope derives the most likely router from the DHCP server, an existing gateway on the same subnet, or a responding address at the start or end of the adapter's subnet. It first renews the DHCP lease; if Windows still has no default route, it adds a persistent default route for the detected gateway. The exact gateway is shown before anything changes.

params.name: Gateway
params.description: Detected router address for this adapter's subnet

snapshot.label: default routes

Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.DestinationPrefix -eq '0.0.0.0/0' } |
  Select-Object DestinationPrefix,NextHop,InterfaceAlias,RouteMetric,InterfaceMetric,Store |
  ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4

ladder.name: Renew the DHCP lease
ladder.description: If the router hands out a gateway by DHCP, this restores it without a manual route.

ladder.name: Add a persistent default route
ladder.description: Adds the detected router as the default gateway for this adapter. Existing default routes on the adapter are replaced.

commands.label: set the detected gateway
commands.script:
param($AdapterName,$Gateway)
Remove-NetRoute -InterfaceAlias $AdapterName -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' -InterfaceAlias $AdapterName -NextHop $Gateway -RouteMetric 0 -Store Persistent -ErrorAction Stop
